summary: Exec tasks and mission-run seats start at normal priority; standing seats stay in background

rules.detail: An exec task, or a seat whose subject a mission run owns, now launches with ST_SEAT_PRIORITY=normal unless it declares ST_SEAT_PRIORITY itself; on macOS it no longer starts under `taskpolicy -b`, on Linux no longer under nice 10 / ionice level 7. Standing seats keep the install's seat_priority (default background).

compatibility.detail: Declaring ST_SEAT_PRIORITY "background" (or FRACTAL_SEAT_PRIORITY) on an exec or run-owned seat keeps the previous behaviour. Running tasks keep the priority they started with.

downtime.detail: Applies to launches after the daemon restarts on the new release.

manual.detail: No user action is required. Installs that set seat_priority only to speed up execs can drop it.

recovery.detail: Roll back the release, or declare ST_SEAT_PRIORITY "background" on affected execs.
